newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Westpac says tough to lift profit.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Westpac says tough to lift profit.

text.p: Westpac Banking Corp said on Tuesday it would be tough to increase absolute profit in the 1996/97 financial year, but that it saw earnings per share a little bit higher because of a planned share buyback.
"It will be tough to make a rise," Westpac managing director Bob Joss told a news conference, when asked whether profits for the year would be flat.
Joss said also that Westpac planned mortgage securitisation issues much greater than the A$340 million completed during 1995/96 (October-September).
He said it would be difficult in the coming year for Westpac to keep its group interest margin up at the 370 basis points reported for the year to September 30, 1996.
Competition from non-bank lenders funded from mortgage origination in the home mortgage market would place a lot of pressure on group margins, he said.
Westpac would look to take some of its own mortgages off balance sheet and continue its mortgage securitisation programme begun in 1995/96.
"It will be more than that (A$340 million)," Joss said of the likely securitisation programme in the current year.
Joss said the near 20 percent fall in profit to A$86 million of Australian Guarantee Corp (AGC) for the year was disappointing, but that he expected the finance unit's results to improve.
"We think we're on track to turn it around," he said.
AGC suffered from increase loan losses from car and personal loans but credit procedures had been altered to rectify the problem.
"I think we'll see a better experience next year. We've already seen better delinquencies (late repayments) in the last few months," he said.
Westpac shares closed 15 cents weaker at A$7.05.
